title: The hot or pulsatile lump: cellulitis, abscess, haematoma or pseudoaneurysm
summary: A red, swollen or pulsatile lump raises one question before anyone reaches for a blade: what is inside it? Learn to separate cellulitis from abscess, make a collection swirl, find the neck of a pseudoaneurysm, and drain safely under ultrasound.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency, acute and urgent care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners and physician associates who assess skin and soft tissue swellings or drain abscesses.
outcomes: Scan a superficial swelling with the right probe, settings and comparison views
Separate cellulitis from abscess, and recognise a collection by its swirl
Use colour and pulsed-wave Doppler to identify haematoma, pseudoaneurysm and true aneurysm
Recognise the lumps which must not be incised, and plan ultrasound-guided drainage safely
references: Gottlieb M, et al. Point-of-care ultrasonography for the diagnosis of skin and soft tissue abscesses: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Annals of Emergency Medicine. 2020;76:67.
